memverses.text: You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do you.
But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.

catechism.a: God is the only living and true God. [He’s the all-glorious, almighty, all-knowing, sovereign Creator and Lord of the whole universe. God is perfect and holy, infinite, eternal, and unchanging.]
Nobody made God.

catechism.q: Has God ever had a beginning?
catechism.a: No, God has always been.
No, God lives forever!

catechism.q: Are there more gods than one?
catechism.a: No, there is only one true God.

catechism.q: In how many persons does this one God exist?
catechism.a: God exists in three persons.

catechism.q: Who are the three persons of God?
catechism.a: The three persons of God are the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.
God is everywhere.
[No, God is a spirit, and He doesn’t have a body like man.] Though I cannot see God, I know He always sees me.
Yes, God knows all things. [Nothing can be hidden from God.]
Yes, God can do all His holy will.
God made me.
I was made to glorify God and enjoy Him forever.
God made all things.

catechism.q: Why did God make all things?
catechism.a: For His own glory.
I can glorify God by loving Him and doing what He commands.
I should glorify God because He made me and takes care of me.
Adam and Eve were our first parents.

catechism.q: What were Adam and Eve like when God made them?
catechism.a: God made them holy and happy.
No, Adam chose to disobey God.

catechism.q: How did God punish Adam’s disobedience?
catechism.a: Adam’s punishment was death and separation from God.
Sin is disobedience [against God’s perfect law by failing to do what God commands or doing what God forbids.]

catechism.q: What happened to Adam and Eve when they sinned?
catechism.a: Instead of being holy and happy, they became sinful and miserable.

catechism.q: What did Adam’s sin do to you?
catechism.a: It made me guilty and sinful.
The wrath and curse of God.

catechism.q: How sinful are you by nature?
catechism.a: I am corrupt in every part of my being.

catechism.q: Can you go to Heaven with a sinful nature?
catechism.a: No, my heart must be changed before I can go to Heaven.

catechism.q: What is this change of heart called?
catechism.a: Regeneration, being “born again.”

catechism.q: Who can change a sinner’s heart?
catechism.a: Only God can change a sinner’s heart.

catechism.q: Who is the Redeemer of God’s elect?
catechism.a: The only Savior of men is the Lord Jesus Christ, [who being the eternal Son of God, became man and so is both God and man in two natures and one person.]
My heart is changed by the Holy Spirit because of the grace of God.
Grace is God’s kindness to us when we deserve punishment.

catechism.q: What work did Christ do to save you?
catechism.a: Christ perfectly kept the law of God and suffered the punishment due for my sins.

catechism.q: Can anyone be saved by his own works?
catechism.a: No one can be saved by his own works.

catechism.q: What do we gain from the work of Christ?
catechism.a: God regenerates, justifies, and sanctifies those who believe in Christ.
Justification is God forgiving all my sins and declaring me to be righteous.
Sanctification is God making me holy in heart and behavior.

catechism.q: What are the two parts of sanctification?
catechism.a: Dying to sin and living to righteousness.
Whoever repents and believes on the Lord Jesus Christ.

catechism.q: What does it mean to repent?
catechism.a: To repent is to be sorry for sin, and to hate and forsake it [because it displeases God.]
Faith in Christ is trusting in Him alone for salvation.

catechism.q: How were people saved before the coming of Christ?
catechism.a: People were saved by believing in a Savior to come.
No, Jesus lived a sinless life.

catechism.q: What kind of death did Christ die?
catechism.a: A painful and shameful death on the cross.

catechism.q: What are the offices Christ fulfilled as the promised Messiah?
catechism.a: Prophet, Priest, and King.
Christ teaches me the will of God.
Christ died for me; He prays for me, [He washed away my every sin.]
Christ rules over me; He defends me; [He will establish His Kingdom on earth.]

catechism.q: Did Christ remain in the tomb?
catechism.a: No, Christ is risen on the third day, [just as He did say.]
Christ is in heaven, [and He’s praying for me;] He sits at the right hand of God.
Yes, He is coming soon.
No one knows when Christ will return.

catechism.q: What happens to a man when he dies?
catechism.a: The body returns to the dust, and the spirit will go to either heaven or hell.

catechism.q: What will happen when Christ returns?
catechism.a: Our bodies will be raised from the dust, and united again with our spirits.

catechism.q: What will happen to the wicked on Judgment day?
catechism.a: The wicked will go down on judgment day and will be cast into the lake of fire.

catechism.q: What will happen to every Christian on the last day?
catechism.a: Every Christian will live with Jesus in the new heavens and the new earth.

catechism.q: Where do we learn to love and obey God?
catechism.a: In the Bible, we learn to love and obey God.
Holy men of God, who were taught and chosen by God, wrote the Bible.
Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul, and mind; [and the second is like it, love your neighbor as yourself.]

catechism.q: Of what use are the ten commandments?
catechism.a: They teach us our duty [to God and our duty to man,] and show us our need for a Savior.
Prayer is praising God [for who He is,] thanking God [for what He’s done,] and asking Him for things [He has promised.]

catechism.q: What guide has Christ given to teach us how to pray?
catechism.a: Christ has given us the Lord’s Prayer to teach us how to pray.
